title: Upper amplitude from finite classical cohomological dimension
statement: Let C be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] and D an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], with chosen unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], injective resolutions and K-injective resolutions [def-sp-kinjective-bridge] in C. Let F : C → D be additive and left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Suppose d is a natural number and R^q F(M) = 0 for every object M and every q > d. For every integer b and L in D(C) whose cohomology vanishes above b, the cohomology of RF(L) vanishes above b+d. No lower bound on L is assumed.

source.place: Tag 07K7, lemma-unbounded-right-derived, part (4)(c), lines 9977-10105; dimension-shifting proof on cycles

proof.text: Represent L by a K-injective complex I with injective components, using the functorial K-injective resolution. The representing isomorphism transports the upper bound b to I.

For k ≥ 0 prove that R^(q+1) F(Z^n I) vanishes if n ≥ b+k and d ≤ q+k. At k=0 use the cohomological-dimension bound. For the successor, exactness of I at n gives the short exact sequence 0 → Z^(n-1) I → I^(n-1) → Z^n I → 0. Since the middle term is F-acyclic, the connecting map injects R^(q+1) F(Z^n I) into R^(q+2) F(Z^(n-1) I). Apply induction. At k=d every cycle in degree n ≥ b+d is F-acyclic.

For m>b+d put n=m-1. The cycles sequence is short exact and Z^n I is F-acyclic; left exactness and the derived connecting sequence show that F preserves this short exact sequence. Preservation of the kernel of I^m → I^(m+1) identifies its image with the kernel, so F(I) is exact at m. Thus F(I) is bounded above by b+d.
The existing K-injective comparison RF(QI) ≅ Q(FI) and the representing isomorphism for L transport this bound to RF(L). The proof includes d=0, negative b, and zero complexes.
